No files were modified.

## Existing checkpoint/session model

The persistent checkpoint API is already a strong fit for “checkpoint as intent source.”

- [api/checkpoint/interfaces.go](C:/Users/gshek/cli-btw/api/checkpoint/interfaces.go) defines:
  - `CheckpointReader.Read/List`
  - `SessionReader.ReadSessionContent`, `ReadSessionMetadataAndPrompts`
  - `PersistentStore`
  - helpers `ReadCheckpoint`, `ReadLatestSessionContent`, and `ReadRawSessionLogForCheckpoint`.
- [api/checkpoint/metadata.go](C:/Users/gshek/cli-btw/api/checkpoint/metadata.go) defines the data contract:
  - `CheckpointSummary`: checkpoint-wide ID, branch, files, sessions, tokens, combined attribution, review/investigation flags.
  - `SessionContent`: `Metadata`, raw `Transcript`, `Prompts`.
  - `Metadata`: session ID, agent/model, `FilesTouched`, `CheckpointTranscriptStart`, `SkillEvents`, summary, attribution, kind, review/investigation context.
  - `SessionFilePaths`: root metadata points to each session’s `metadata.json`, `full.jsonl`, optional compact transcript, and `prompt.txt`.
- A checkpoint stores the complete transcript available at that checkpoint; `Metadata.CheckpointTranscriptStart` identifies the portion attributable to that individual checkpoint. This is exactly the distinction the audit needs: whole-session context versus checkpoint-scoped intent.
- Persistent read topology is centralized in [cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/open.go](C:/Users/gshek/cli-btw/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/open.go), `checkpoint.Open`. Its `kindRoutingStore` reads both legacy branch-backed IDs and refs-backed ULIDs transparently.
- The committed storage implementations are [persistent.go](C:/Users/gshek/cli-btw/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/persistent.go) and [refs_store.go](C:/Users/gshek/cli-btw/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/refs_store.go). Do not read `entire/checkpoints/v1` directly: `checkpoint.Open` handles current backend selection, migration, and remote-on-demand reads.
- Live session state is separate and mutable: [cmd/entire/cli/session/state.go](C:/Users/gshek/cli-btw/cmd/entire/cli/session/state.go), `session.State`, persisted as `.git/entire-sessions/<session-id>.json` by `StateStore`. It tracks turn IDs, touched files, checkpoint offsets, and pending checkpoint IDs. It is useful for active/pending work, but not the authoritative source for an audit of committed work.
- The durable lifecycle model is also represented in [cmd/entire/cli/strategy/session.go](C:/Users/gshek/cli-btw/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/session.go), `strategy.Session` / `strategy.Checkpoint`.

## Existing command seams

Cobra construction is centralized in [cmd/entire/cli/root.go](C:/Users/gshek/cli-btw/cmd/entire/cli/root.go), `NewRootCmd()`.

The natural parent is already present:

- [cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint_group.go](C:/Users/gshek/cli-btw/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint_group.go), `newCheckpointGroupCmd()`
  - currently registers `list`, `resume`, `explain`, `tokens`, `search`, and experimental `policy`.
- [cmd/entire/cli/explain.go](C:/Users/gshek/cli-btw/cmd/entire/cli/explain.go), `newExplainCmd()` is the closest behavioral sibling:
  - resolves checkpoint ID, commit SHA, or checkpoint prefix;
  - supports `--session-index`;
  - opens stores with blob/ref/metadata remote fetchers;
  - finds Git links with `getAssociatedCommits`;
  - uses `loadCheckpointForExplain`.
- [cmd/entire/cli/explain_export.go](C:/Users/gshek/cli-btw/cmd/entire/cli/explain_export.go) is the best existing machine interface:
  - `runExplainExport`
  - `resolveExplainCheckpointID`
  - `runExplainStreamTranscript`
  - `resolveSessionIndex`
  - `entire checkpoint explain <id> --json`
  - `entire checkpoint explain <id> --transcript [--session-index N]`

The commit ↔ checkpoint link is `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>`. Parsing lives in [cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go](C:/Users/gshek/cli-btw/cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go), `ParseCheckpoint` and `ParseAllCheckpoints`. For an audit, prefer `ParseAllCheckpoints`: squash commits may retain multiple checkpoint trailers, while `getAssociatedCommits` currently uses the single-value parser.

## Plugins, extensions, and external agents

There are three distinct mechanisms:

| Mechanism | Implementation | Checkpoint access |
|---|---|---|
| Native Cobra command | `NewRootCmd` / `newCheckpointGroupCmd` | Direct, complete |
| External command plugin | [cmd/entire/cli/plugin.go](C:/Users/gshek/cli-btw/cmd/entire/cli/plugin.go), `MaybeRunPlugin`, `resolvePlugin`, `runPlugin` | None beyond subprocess/public CLI |
| External agent protocol | [cmd/entire/cli/agent/external](C:/Users/gshek/cli-btw/cmd/entire/cli/agent/external) | Full lifecycle integration |

External commands are `entire-<name>` executables on `PATH`; built-ins win, `entire-agent-*` names are reserved, and execution inherits stdio. The managed installer is the built-in `entire plugin` group in [plugin_group.go](C:/Users/gshek/cli-btw/cmd/entire/cli/plugin_group.go). The contract only supplies `ENTIRE_CLI_VERSION`, optional `ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT`, and a per-plugin data directory. It does not supply checkpoint ID, transcript, Git range, or graph results.

The repository documentation explicitly distinguishes this limitation in [docs/architecture/external-commands.md](C:/Users/gshek/cli-btw/docs/architecture/external-commands.md): external commands have no checkpoint protocol; external agents do.

External agents are different: `entire-agent-<name>` binaries are discovered by `external.DiscoverAndRegister` in [discovery.go](C:/Users/gshek/cli-btw/cmd/entire/cli/agent/external/discovery.go), speak JSON subcommands through `external.Agent` in [external.go](C:/Users/gshek/cli-btw/cmd/entire/cli/agent/external/external.go), and are adapted to `agent.Agent` in [capabilities.go](C:/Users/gshek/cli-btw/cmd/entire/cli/agent/external/capabilities.go). This is for capture/lifecycle integrations, not a good first home for a post-hoc audit command.

There is no existing in-process Entire Graph integration. The repository only recognizes `entire-graph` as a possible external plugin/dependency in the plugin documentation. An audit implementation should treat `entire graph` as an optional local executable, invoke it through a bounded subprocess, and degrade clearly if unavailable.

## Recommended smallest viable implementation

Add a native, read-only command:

```text
entire checkpoint audit <checkpoint-id|commit-sha>
```

Register it from `newCheckpointGroupCmd()` beside `explain`.

Implement initially as `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint_audit.go`, in package `cli`, so it can directly reuse the existing unexported resolution/read plumbing:

1. Resolve ID/commit using `resolveExplainCheckpointID` or extract a small shared resolver from [explain_export.go](C:/Users/gshek/cli-btw/cmd/entire/cli/explain_export.go).
2. Open via `newExplainCheckpointLookup` / `checkpoint.Open`, never by direct branch/ref traversal.
3. Read `CheckpointSummary`; read all relevant sessions using `ReadSessionContent`.
4. Construct an intent packet from:
   - `SessionContent.Prompts` as primary human intent;
   - transcript events as supporting evidence;
   - `Metadata.CheckpointTranscriptStart` to distinguish this checkpoint’s work from prior session context;
   - `Metadata.FilesTouched` / `CheckpointSummary.FilesTouched` as declared scope;
   - agent/model, skill events, and review/investigation fields as provenance.
5. Resolve implementation evidence:
   - checkpoint-linked commits via the trailer;
   - changed-file list and patches from Git;
   - current source at the audited commit or current checkout;
   - focused tests inferred from changed files and/or explicitly selected by a later `--test` option.
6. Invoke `entire graph search` and, when symbols are identified, `entire graph impact` against the audited repository. Return the exact graph evidence used in the report.
7. Emit a deterministic JSON report first (`--json`), with verdicts such as `supported`, `missing`, `out_of_scope`, and `unverifiable`. A prose renderer can follow.

The most important implementation choice is to make this native rather than begin as `entire-audit`. A plugin can prototype by composing:

```text
entire checkpoint explain <id> --json
entire checkpoint explain <id> --transcript
git …
entire graph …
```

…but it would duplicate checkpoint/commit resolution, remote fetch behavior, session selection, and error handling. A native `checkpoint audit` command gets those semantics for free and remains backend-agnostic.

Suggested first tests:

- `checkpoint_audit_test.go`: hex and ULID checkpoint resolution, checkpoint ID versus commit target, multi-session selection, absent transcript, no linked commit, JSON stability.
- Reuse patterns in [cmd/entire/cli/explain_export_test.go](C:/Users/gshek/cli-btw/cmd/entire/cli/explain_export_test.go) for export/session-index behavior and [cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/routing_store_test.go](C:/Users/gshek/cli-btw/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/routing_store_test.go) for backend routing.
- Include a squash-commit regression using `trailers.ParseAllCheckpoints`, not only `ParseCheckpoint`.

- `newCheckpointGroupCmd` in `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint_group.go` for native Cobra registration.
- `resolveExplainCheckpointID`, `newExplainCheckpointLookup`, and `resolveSessionIndex` from `explain_export.go` / `explain.go` for prefix-or-commit resolution, remote-aware store opening, and multi-session selection.

I’ll create `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint_audit.go` and modify only `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint_group.go`. I’ll leave findings empty rather than fabricate verdicts, retain explicit evidence warnings, and run Entire Graph as an optional `entire graph search` subprocess using the recovered intent.

- `resolveExplainCheckpointID`, `newExplainCheckpointLookup`, `resolveSessionIndex` for checkpoint/commit resolution and backend-aware reads.
- `checkpoint.ReadCheckpoint` and `ReadSessionContent` for checkpoint intent/session context.
- `trailers.ParseAllCheckpoints` for squash-safe checkpoint-to-commit linkage.
- Go-git from the explain lookup for reachable linked commits and parent→commit diffs.
- Cobra registration in `newCheckpointGroupCmd`.

Changed:

- [checkpoint_group.go](C:/Users/gshek/cli-btw/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint_group.go) — registers `audit`.
- [checkpoint_audit.go](C:/Users/gshek/cli-btw/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint_audit.go) — new native evidence collector.

Data flow:

```text
target → explain resolver → persistent checkpoint/session read
       → intent packet
       → trailer-linked Git commits → diffs/files/changed test files
       → optional Entire Graph search → normalized JSON/prose report
```

The command is intentionally read-only and does not invoke Gemini or fabricate verdicts. `findings` is an empty array until a separate audit/evaluation layer is added; evidence warnings explicitly report missing Git linkage or unavailable Graph evidence.

I corrected the supplied skeleton’s invalid imports/signatures and avoided deriving commits from checkpoint metadata, which does not contain commit messages. Graph evidence uses optional `entire graph search`; its text output is preserved in a JSON envelope.
